_about: 16-bit code/data patches applied by build.py stage 3c when 'enabled' is true. Each checks the current halfword(s) ('expect') first; 'expect'/'value' are one halfword ("0x2305") or a run of halfwords ("01DE 012B ..."). namelen-*: naming-screen length limits raised from the hack's 5 (Japanese base, IPKJ) to the US values (7 trainer names, 10 Pokemon); the save buffers already have the US sizes. Enabled after the user's in-game check (7-char trainer names, 10-char nicknames). naming-*: English naming keyboard (localisation necessity, D-1002): the hack's pinyin page is gone. Tab 1 (page 0, the page the screen opens on) is ABC = the hack's ABC layout (A-M, N-Z, a-m, n-z, 0-9) in Western letter codes; tab 3 (page 2, was the full-width ABC page, whose letters render 8-11 px wide in the English message fonts) is QWE = a plain uppercase QWERTY page; tabs 2 (abc) and 4 (1/music note) are the hack's. Tab labels: graphics patch naming_labels_en.png (gfx.py make-naming-labels). See work/notes/hardcoded_text.md. msgload-*: heap fixes (work/notes/heap_audit.md). The English message banks are 1.5-3x the Chinese ones; screens that load whole banks into a fixed heap ran out of memory (summary: switch Pokemon on the skills page crashed; bag: 108 bytes to spare). NewMsgDataFromNarc(type, narc, bank, heap) at 0x0200BA98: type 0 loads the whole bank into the heap, type 1 keeps a NARC handle and reads each line when asked. 'movs r0, #0' -> 'movs r0, #1' at the call site; same text, only where it is read from. antipiracy-*: Nintendo DS Protect in overlay114 (RAM 0x02263200): its six entry points are stubbed to return the genuine-cart values (0,1,0,1,0,1), so flashcarts and loaders that fail the card-mirror or MAC checks no longer leak heap 3 at Continue and on every menu, or fill the task queue until the game freezes (work/notes/hardware_support.md).

All screens: NewMsgDataFromNarc at 0x0200BA98 stores type 1 whatever the caller asked: 'adds r5, r0, #0' -> 'movs r5, #1' at 0x0200BA9A. Every text bank is read line by line; none is loaded whole into a screen heap any more (149 call sites in rc3). Every MsgData function handles both types, and nothing outside them reads a loaded bank. The msgload-summary/bag patches are kept as a second layer.

PC box top screen (D-1511): window templates at 0x12E9C (8 bytes each: bg, x, y, w, h, pal, base). The species-name window 04 08 05 07 (56 px, Japanese base) -> 04 08 05 08 (64 px, ends at the gender icon at x 128) so 10-character names fit; the bg-4 base tiles of the next windows move up by 2 (0x77->0x79 ... 0xC9->0xCB). The whole run equals the USA table (US ov14 0x12BB4).

DS Protect 'any bad' entry, flashcart card-mirror check (raw card-bus B7 reads of ROM 0x1000-0x1400 vs 0x8000-0x8400, CRC32) + integrity check; returns 1 if any check detects. Called by ov1 field init, ov28 and ov5. Stubbed to 'mov r0,#0; bx lr': 0 is the value the untouched hack returns on a genuine cart (and in DeSmuME). Original 'push {r4-r10,lr}; sub sp,#0x80'. The entry takes r0 = callback and is called by Thumb blx, so 'bx lr' returns correctly; the stub skips the callback, which on the genuine path is a bare 'bx lr' (the 'detected' callbacks are 1000-byte heap-3 leaks). The integrity checks cover only the four check bodies, not the entry prologues. Same 8 bytes as Bradams' Speedoption ov114. See work/notes/hardware_support.md.
